text:
maria: heads up — noticed reproducible mem growth on int8 kvcache for longctx test (50k tokens). baseline BF16 stays flat; INT8 ramps up ~1.3GB over 30min on staging. :eyes:

devon: can you paste the telemetry? which allocator / page counts look off?

maria: quick dump from profiler run:
```
# run id: run-20240412-03
kv_pages_total: 15328
kv_pages_used: 15002
kv_frag_slots_pct: 13.1
kv_allocated_mb: 6812
kv_active_mb: 5710
mem_growth_30m: 1396MB
avg_latency_p95: 38ms
```
observed: steady page allocs & lots of small free holes (fragmentation).

ajay: interesting — int8 reduces model footprint but increases number of small allocations due to page packing / smaller per-slot usage. fragmentation explains growth. did you try compaction?

maria: tried immediate compaction every 5k slots, reduces growth but thrashes the CPU — p95 jumps ~2-3ms. results: mem_growth_30m -> ~220MB but p95 up.

irina: is this the same path as the residency/eviction change from last month? could be interaction with reuse/warmup heuristics.

maria: yep same stack. additionally noticed warmup writes create transient tiny KV pages that are not coalesced with adjacent free slots.

devon: two quick experiments to reproduce: 1) run longctx synthetic with int8 and disable slot_reuse; 2) run with slot_coalesce_on_free=true. numbers?

maria: results:
```
# experiment A (slot_reuse=false)
mem_growth_30m: 1720MB
p95: 36ms
# experiment B (slot_coalesce_on_free=true)
mem_growth_30m: 210MB
p95: 40.2ms
```
so coalescing helps a lot for mem but increases p95 slightly.

ajay: tradeoff is expected. could we do background compaction with low-priority threads + rate limit to avoid p95 impact? or trigger compaction only when free-frag > threshold?

irina: also measure quality: int8 key/value quantization might slightly affect logits. what did eval show?

maria: ran the eval-set 10k prompts: int8 baseline (no compaction) vs bf16: avg ppl +0.6%, accuracy on QA drop ~0.3pts. with coalesce/compaction same quant params — no diffs vs int8 baseline (so compaction doesn't change model quality).

devon: good — compaction is only memory/layout side-effect. given p95 hit, background compaction with throttling looks promising. we should consider changing page size or slot packing heuristics for INT8 mode so we reduce number of tiny free segments.

ajay: another angle: kernel selection. if INT8 runtime uses different matmul kernel, check if coalescing interacts with our AVX2/AVX512 allocation patterns. small allocs could change alignment -> kernel perf jitter. run kernel-flags A/B.

maria: will run kernel A/B with coalesce on/off and capture perf counters. initial micro-run: coalesce on + kernel-fast gave ~+1.9% latency vs baseline kernel but mem growth fixed.

irina: logging/telemetry asks: add metrics for frag_pct_by_page_size and compaction_cpu_seconds so we can tune. also add a counter for compaction_ops_triggered.

maria: created a small patch to add those metrics and a feature-flag for background_compaction_rate. will push canary to staging today.

infra-bot: deploy started: canary/kv-coalesce-rate-limited -> staging (sha abc123). ETA 15m.

devon: next steps: 1) run longctx 2h canary with int8 + bg compaction; 2) run kernel A/B with aligned alloc config; 3) evaluate quality delta on eval set. assign: maria -> 1, devon -> 2, irina -> 3. timeline: today/tomorrow. :thumbsup:

maria: thanks — will post results in this thread. if we see sustained mem growth with background compaction, plan B is to increase page_size for int8 mode only (fewer pages -> less frag) and evaluate memory vs latency tradeoffs.
